key_insight: A pretrained autoregressive language model can be converted into a fast, standalone multi-token predictor by training it to self-distill its own next-token behavior into multi-token outputs, avoiding auxiliary speculator models and complex pipelines.
problem_solved: Reduces inference latency and system complexity caused by single-step next-token generation and multi-model speculative decoding approaches, enabling simpler, faster deployment of language models.
method: Online self-distillation: continue training the pretrained autoregressive model so it predicts multiple future tokens in one forward pass using its own predictions as targets.
Multi-token objective: replace or augment the standard single-token loss with a multi-token prediction loss that encourages accurate short sequence outputs.
No auxiliary models or special inference code: retain the original model architecture/implementation while changing only the training objective to produce a standalone multi-token predictor.
impact: Enables substantial inference speedups and simpler deployment for practitioners without adding extra models or complex decoding pipelines; useful for latency-sensitive applications and production systems.
visual_elements: Before vs After pipeline diagram: (left) autoregressive single-token loop + speculative speculator, (right) single multi-token model producing k tokens per step
Training schematic: teacher (original model) generating targets → student (same-architecture model) learning multi-token outputs via self-distillation
Speed/throughput chart: tokens-per-second or latency comparison between standard decoding, speculative decoding, and the distilled multi-token model
Illustrative icon set: single-model-only deployment, no extra services, and a speedometer showing lower latency
paper_authors: John Kirchenbauer, Abhimanyu Hans, Brian Bartoldson, Micah Goldblum, Ashwinee Panda
